troubleshooting.problem: approve says watch-only mode is on
troubleshooting.expected_output: refused: watch-only mode is on; nothing may act
troubleshooting.recovery: This is the default, on purpose. For one test, run the command with WATCH_ONLY=false. Only false, 0, no or off turn it off; a typo leaves it on.

troubleshooting.problem: The same approval is refused the second time
troubleshooting.example_input: WATCH_ONLY=false python -m safe_operator approve 1 --by owner, twice
troubleshooting.recovery: An approval runs once. Propose the action again if you need it again.
Only actions registered in the catalog can be proposed. Add a new one in actions.py with a strict params table, starting at Tier.ASK.

troubleshooting.expected_output: sales_today: UNKNOWN ... SALES_API_KEY is not set, so sales can't be read
troubleshooting.recovery: Correct until you connect a source: no number is shown when it can't be read. Set a restricted, read-only key and point SALES_API_URL at your provider (collectors/sales.py).

troubleshooting.expected_output: website: UNKNOWN ... could not reach https://example.invalid (ConnectError)
troubleshooting.recovery: The site couldn't be reached from your machine. Check the address and your connection; the check never reports a site it can't read as OK.

review_demo.request: A customer asked when their order ships. The operator proposes reply_to_customer for thread t1, with the reason "customer asked when it ships" and a one-hour expiry.
review_demo.draft: dry run: would reply on thread t1 with: Thanks, it ships Monday.
review_demo.review_step: The proposal waits in the pending list with its reason and expiry. Nothing has run. While watch-only mode is on, even an approval is refused.
review_demo.on_approve: With watch-only off: "approved #1 by owner; handing it to the executor", then "done: (demo) replied on thread t1". A second approval is refused: it is claimed.
review_demo.on_silence: expires in 3600s. If nobody answers, it simply does not run.
review_demo.limits: The demo actions describe what they would do and touch nothing. The gate covers actions that go through the executor; it doesn't check whether the reply says the right thing. You read the dry run before you approve.

faq.q: Can my child use Claude?
faq.a: No. Claude is for adults 18 and over, and you may not share your account with anyone, including your children. In these courses, only an adult ever types or speaks to Claude. faq.q: Do I need to pay for Claude?

faq.q: Do I need to pay for n8n?

faq.q: Is this legal, medical or financial advice?
faq.a: No. The courses teach you to use AI for questions, and to take decisions to a doctor, pharmacist, lawyer, bank or adviser.

faq.q: I bought this for my parent. Can they use my account?
faq.a: No. Claude accounts can't be shared. They set up their own free account, on their own phone, in Lesson 3.1. You can sit next to them while they do it.

Everyday AI for Adults comes as a zip with the PDF, a folder of n8n workflow files (JSON) and a Claude Skill. Open the PDFs on a phone, tablet or computer, or print them. For Safe and Simple AI 60+, printing the PDF is recommended.

faq.q: Does it send texts or emails?
faq.a: No. Every workflow writes a draft to a file and answers sent: false. There is no sending node in any file. Chapter 9 explains how to add one later, and why to add it last.

faq.q: Do I need n8n Cloud or a paid plan?
faq.a: No. The pack runs on n8n's free self-hosted edition with Docker, on your own computer or server. n8n's licence allows using it for your own business and for automation services you offer to clients.

faq.q: Do I need to know how to code?
faq.a: No. Every change is editing a short list or a placeholder such as [Business name] inside a box. The code in the workflows is already written and explained node by node.

faq.q: Will it work with my form, phone system or job tracker?
faq.a: It works with anything that can send a web request (a webhook) to a URL, which most form tools and business phone systems can. If yours can't, you can still add a row with one command and get the draft; the guide shows how.

faq.q: Are the workflow files really tested?
faq.a: They were imported, run and exported again on n8n 2.40.7 on 1 Oct 2026. The appendix lists exactly what was sent and what came back, including a deliberately malicious lead that was escaped correctly.

products.intro: A printable workbook, by the owner. AI tools can now copy a voice, make up a video and write a message with no mistakes in it, so the old clues are not much help. benefits: Choose a family safe word the right way, and agree that asking for it is never rude.
Hang up on any call that asks for money, a code or personal details, and call back on a number you wrote down while you were calm.
Keep one clear list of what never goes into an AI tool, a text or a phone call.
Check any unexpected call, text, email or video against six stop signs on one page.
Open the conversation with an older parent without it sounding like "you are getting old", and set their phone corner up in one visit.
Run short, announced family drills so the words are already there when you need them.
Know who to contact, in what order, if a scam gets through, with the official reporting sites and helplines already printed and your own numbers filled in.

audience: People who want to start selling online with one small, real thing rather than a plan for ten.
Anyone curious about clipping who wants the version that doesn't get a channel removed.
People who already know something useful and haven't turned it into a product yet.
Anyone thinking about a dropshipping store who wants to know what they're responsible for first.
not_for: Anyone looking for a figure for what they'll earn. There isn't one in the course, and no method here promises results.
Anyone who wants to repost other people's videos, resell bundles of other people's templates, or list products they've never seen.
Anyone who wants an AI to run a business unattended. This course has AI draft and check; you decide, and money out is always your own click.
People after legal, tax or financial advice. The course points to your own country's guidance for sellers and says where the rules are yours to check.
products.notice: Sold to adults 18+. The course teaches methods and describes what the author does; it doesn't promise income or results.

faq.q: Is this a video course or an ebook?
faq.a: Both exist, with the same lessons: one narrated video per lesson, or one PDF, or both together. Choose on this page.

faq.q: Will this tell me how much I'll make?
faq.a: No. The course contains no earnings figures. It teaches three methods and how to read your own numbers from their sources.

faq.q: Do I need to pay for tools?
faq.a: No subscription is needed to follow the lessons. Claude's free plan covers the writing, the video tool used for cutting is free, and a payment account charges per sale.

faq.q: Is clipping other people's videos allowed?
faq.a: Only with permission. Module 1 is built on one rule: cut only footage the owner has put up for clippers, with the campaign's rules saved.

faq.q: Do I have to do all three?
faq.a: No. The modules stand alone, and the last lesson helps you pick one lane for your first month.

faq.q: How do I get it?
faq.a: After payment you land on your access page with your download. Bookmark it; it makes fresh download links each time you open it.

products.refund: 14-day money-back guarantee: if it isn't useful, email us within 14 days of purchase for a full refund, no questions asked.
products.licence: One purchase covers one household: everyone who lives in the buyer's home may use the guides and printables. Please don't resell or share them publicly. The buyer must be an adult. We never ask for a child's name, age or email.
products.pairs_reason: Sell With AI keeps AI to drafting and checking. Build a Safe AI Operator shows how to build the agent that does that with controls you can inspect: a closed list of actions, tiers set in code, and approvals that are claimed once and expire if nobody answers.

products.level_detail: Needs a computer, a Claude account and a payment account.

finish.deliverable: One selling lane set up end to end. For a digital product: a page that describes only what's inside, a payment link, and delivery only after the payment provider confirms. For all three lanes: a weekly report where every number has a source and a time, or says unknown.
finish.preview: Lesson 3.5's drafting instruction: the model drafts each customer reply from the order record and your policy pages only, leaves a gap where a fact is missing, marks chargebacks, lawyers, injuries and safety problems urgent without drafting a reply, and never promises a refund, a replacement or a date.

paid_adds.detail: 27 lessons in 4 modules, each ending with one thing to do.
Narrated videos, a PDF, or both.

review_demo.request: A customer message: where is my order, a question before buying, something's wrong, a return or cancellation, or everything else.
review_demo.draft: The model says which of the five kinds it is and drafts a reply from the order record and your policies, with a gap for any missing fact.
review_demo.review_step: The model writes; you send. Every reply, for at least the first few weeks.
review_demo.on_approve: You send it yourself, and any commitment is yours to make.
review_demo.limits: Never automated: paying the supplier, refunds and replacements, replies that commit you to anything, and anything touching a dispute, a safety complaint or a legal threat.

routes.title: Learn together: an older learner and a family member
routes.people: Two adults: an older learner and a family member, at one table or by phone. Claude is for adults 18 and over, so only adults use the Claude lessons; a teenager can join the workbook's Drill 7, never Claude.

steps.title: First sitting: make the plan
steps.who: Both, at the kitchen table, with the workbook printed
steps.do: Read Parts 1 to 5 together, choose your safe word out loud, write your callback list, run two drills, fill in the "If it happens" page and put the cards up. The workbook's own timetable for this sitting adds up to about an hour and a half.
steps.source: Products/Family AI-Scam Defense Workbook/workbook/Part 0 - Start here.md

steps.title: Second sitting: the older learner's own Claude account
steps.who: The older learner types; the family member sits beside them
steps.do: Safe and Simple AI 60+, Lesson 0.1, then Lesson 3.1: the learner creates a free Claude account on their own phone with their own email. Accounts can't be shared.
steps.source: Products/AI for Every Age/seniors/Lesson 3.1 - Create your Claude account.md

steps.title: Practise the call that sounds like family
steps.who: The family member reads the caller's lines; the learner answers
steps.do: Safe and Simple AI 60+, Lesson 6.2: six steps with a made-up call. Ask for the family word, say "I'll call you right back", hang up, and call back on a number you saved yourself.
steps.source: Products/AI for Every Age/seniors/Lesson 6.2 - Voice-clone and family emergency scams.md

steps.title: If you live far apart: a drill by phone
steps.do: Agree the day and time first, say "This is a drill" at the start and the end, and ring back straight away as yourself to ask how it felt. Drills 1 and 2 work this way.
steps.source: Products/Family AI-Scam Defense Workbook/workbook/Part 7 - Family drills.md

steps.title: Keep it going
steps.do: Write a line in the drill log each time you practise, and do the yearly check on Page G.
steps.source: Products/Family AI-Scam Defense Workbook/workbook/Part 9 - Pages to keep by the phone.md

boundaries: Every drill is announced and starts with "This is a drill." Never test anyone with a call they are not expecting.
Use the made-up names in the scripts: never your real bank, real amounts or your real safe word.
The workbook gives your family a plan made ahead of time. It says on its first page that it can't promise to stop every scam.
